correctness.rationale: For every unchosen cell, the 2-domination condition is exactly \(r_i+c_j\ge2\). The lower bound splits exhaustively according to whether a zero column exists, yielding \(|D|\ge n\) or \(|D|\ge2m\), while matching constructions achieve the smaller bound. Equality analysis gives the stated minimum-set families, and inclusion-exclusion gives the boundary count. Direct exhaustive verification for all \(1\le m\le n\le4\) reproduces both minimum sizes and counts.

originality.rationale: The closest recent primary source proves the triangular Young-domination formula only for Hamming squares, so its \(a=2\) result is the \(m=n\) specialization. The closest Cartesian-product 2-domination paper studies total 2-domination, a different invariant. published-finding corpus and web searches using Hamming-rectangle, rook-graph, Cartesian-product, T_2, phase-transition, and minimizer-count formulations found no result covering the rectangular ordinary 2-domination theorem. The inaccessible full text of the 2009 square-rook predecessor remains an explicit residual risk.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification for the first nontrivial threshold in a two-parameter family emphasized by a recent paper. The exact phase transition \(n=2m\) changes the structure of every optimizer, and the closed optimizer counts add reusable structural information beyond the square value. It is not a routine numerical increment or an arbitrary slice.
